Read it. Here's where things stand:

## OpenChoreo v1.2.1 (`22-openchoreo`) — 8 of 20 Fleet paths live

**Working now:** Control plane deployed and healthy over HTTPS — `openchoreo.ash4d.com` (Backstage portal) and `api.openchoreo.ash4d.com/health` both 200, real Let's Encrypt cert to 2026-10-28. Fleet GitRepo `lab-openchoreo` at 8/8 bundles ready. Merged to `main` (PR #16, `4604268`), tree clean.

**Next step:** enable path 9, **Thunder** (the OIDC provider — nothing in the portal can authenticate without it). Read the live `spec.paths`, append `22-openchoreo/thunder`, patch back the full list, wait for 9/9, then confirm `thunder.ash4d.com` stops 404ing. The current 404 is expected, not a bug.

**Key traps flagged for the remaining 12 paths:**
- **Manual bootstrap before paths 10, 13, 15** — copy the control plane's cluster-gateway CA into the three plane namespaces (command in `22-openchoreo/README.md`). Skipping it strands `cluster-agent` in `ContainerCreating` with no useful log signal.
- **Post-install hook race** — plane charts' bootstrap Jobs run before the admission webhook has endpoints. A first-install "context deadline exceeded" may self-heal; check for Job retry before intervening.
- **Memory** — node was at 74% (48/64 GiB) before any of this. Enable paths 16–19 one at a time, `kubectl top node` between each; drop `observability-metrics` first if tight.
- **Unverified assumption** — `data-plane-extras/ingress.yaml` and `observability-extras/ingress.yaml` hardcode Service name `gateway-default`, confirmed only in the control plane namespace.

**Open, undecided:** workflow templates (builds can't run end-to-end without them), Harbor vs the throwaway `registry:2`, two default StorageClasses cluster-wide, and rotating the committed fixture credentials before anything leaves the LAN.

`22-openchoreo/README.md` is the authoritative runbook — install order, prerequisites, bootstrap, rollback.

## Bootstrap: propagating the cluster-gateway CA

**The one manual step, and the most likely thing to go wrong.**

Each plane's `cluster-agent` verifies the control plane's `cluster-gateway`
against a ConfigMap named `cluster-gateway-ca` **in its own namespace**. The CA
is minted by cert-manager in `openchoreo-control-plane` and does not exist
until path 8 has run — so it cannot be committed here.

Run this once, after path 8 and before the plane agents start (paths 10, 13, 15):

```bash
CA=$(kubectl -n openchoreo-control-plane get secret cluster-gateway-ca \
       -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64 -d)

for ns in openchoreo-data-plane openchoreo-workflow-plane openchoreo-observability-plane; do
  kubectl create namespace "$ns" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
  kubectl create configmap cluster-gateway-ca --from-literal=ca.crt="$CA" \
    -n "$ns" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
done
```

**Symptom if you skip it:** the agent pod sits in `ContainerCreating` with a
`MountVolume.SetUp failed ... configmap "cluster-gateway-ca" not found` event.
Not a crashloop, and nothing in the OpenChoreo logs mentions it.

Redo it if the control plane's `cluster-gateway-ca` Certificate is ever
reissued — the ConfigMap is a copy, not a reference, and nothing re-syncs it.

*Registration*, by contrast, **is** declarative: the v1.2.1 CRDs accept
`clientCA.secretKeyRef` with a cross-namespace `namespace`, so `registration/`
references each plane's CA instead of inlining PEM the way upstream's
installer does. That is why there is one bootstrap step here and not four.

## Credentials

=== thunder/fleet.yaml ===
# Fleet bundle — Thunder / ThunderID (Helm), the OIDC identity provider.
#
# OpenChoreo does not authenticate users itself. The control plane's API
# server, Backstage, the observer and the CLI are all OIDC clients of Thunder,
# configured in ../control-plane/values.yaml under `security.oidc`. Nothing in
# the portal works without it.
#
# Chart 0.28.0 from oci://ghcr.io/asgardeo/helm-charts/thunder — note this is
# the Asgardeo chart repo, NOT ghcr.io/openchoreo. Version matches OpenChoreo
# v1.2's installer pin.
#
# ORDERING: Thunder renders its own HTTPRoute attached to `gateway-default` in

- **A `${...}` anywhere in a values file is a Fleet template, and a bundle that

  pre-processes helm values as a Go template with `${` `}` delimiters, so any

  `targeting error` on the GitRepo, not a deploy error:


  Fix is `helm.disablePreProcess: true` in that bundle's `fleet.yaml`. Cost is

  templating — none here do. Hit `22-openchoreo/thunder` (34 KB embedded
  bootstrap script, 61 expansions) and pre-empted on
  `22-openchoreo/observability-events`. **Grep `\${` across a vendored values
  file before enabling its path** — `helm template` does not catch this,
  because the collision is with Fleet, not Helm.

# Fleet GitRepo — OpenChoreo.
#
# This is the Fleet `GitRepo` CUSTOM RESOURCE (gitrepos.fleet.cattle.io), not a
# git repository: it points Fleet at the existing lab-fleet repo and tells it
# which paths to render. It lives on the RANCHER CONTROLLER
# (192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`), so it is not part of any bundle here.
#
#   kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-openchoreo.yaml
#
# ─── This one breaks the lab-<namespace> convention, deliberately ────────────
# Every other GitRepo here owns exactly one namespace. OpenChoreo spans SEVEN
# (openchoreo-control-plane, -data-plane, -workflow-plane, -observability-plane,
# thunder, openbao, external-secrets) and they are not independently useful: a
# data plane with no control plane is nothing, and the planes register with
# each other over mTLS. Splitting them into seven GitRepos would give seven
# knobs that must always be turned together, and would scatter one product's
# rollout across seven files.
#
# So this is one GitRepo per PRODUCT, staged by `spec.paths` — the same
# mechanism `lab-ai` uses, for the same reason.
#
# ─── 🔴 THIS FILE IS STAGE 1 ONLY. RE-APPLYING IT LATER RESETS spec.paths ────
# `paths` below holds the FIRST path only. The remaining nineteen are patched
# in one at a time (see gitrepos/README.md and 22-openchoreo/README.md).
#
# That means: once you have widened the live GitRepo, DO NOT `kubectl apply -f`
# this file again — it will narrow `spec.paths` straight back to one entry.
# FLEET-WIRING.md records this exact mistake being made on lab-lab-memory on
# 2026-07-30, where re-applying a GitRepo file to add `pollingInterval` silently
# reverted a hand-narrowed `spec.paths` and restarted a failing retry loop.
#
# Narrowing is not a rollback either. For `22-openchoreo/control-plane` in
# particular, removing the path uninstalls the release and takes 36 CRDs and
# every OpenChoreo object in the cluster with it. Use `spec.paused: true`.
#
# ─── Fresh install, not an adoption ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Unlike almost everything else in this repo, none of these paths adopts an
# existing release — nothing OpenChoreo-related was on the cluster beforehand.
# So the SSA field-ownership pre-flight in FLEET-WIRING.md does not apply here:
# there is no `helm` field manager to hand over from. What replaces it is
# ordering and prerequisites, which are strict. Read 22-openchoreo/README.md
# before the first apply — in particular the cluster-gateway CA bootstrap,
# which is the one step Fleet cannot do.
apiVersion: fleet.cattle.io/v1alpha1
kind: GitRepo
metadata:
  name: lab-openchoreo
  namespace: fleet-default
spec:
  repo: https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet
  branch: main
  # Explicit polling interval. Fleet's default is 15s, but this cluster's
  # gitjob runs with `gitjob.syncPeriod: 2h` (a Rancher fleet-chart value), and
  # on 2026-07-30 four GitRepos went dormant for 28+ minutes after a single
  # transient `context deadline exceeded` against github.com -- they only
  # recovered when an external write forced a reconcile. Stating the interval
  # here bounds how stale a repo can get and makes the intent reviewable in git
  # rather than depending on a controller-wide default. See FLEET-WIRING.md.
  pollingInterval: 60s
  paths:
    # STAGE 1 ONLY — the other nineteen are patched in one at a time.
    # NOTE `22-openchoreo` itself must NEVER appear in this list: a nested
    # fleet.yaml deploys as soon as its parent path is adopted, so adding the
    # parent would deploy all twenty bundles at once.
    - 22-openchoreo/external-secrets
  # `ash4d-lab` is a bespoke label already on the sdf1 cluster (c-nnzn9). Chosen
  # over management.cattle.io/cluster-name, which Rancher owns and may rewrite.
  # Do NOT reuse site=ash4d — that belonged to a deleted junk cluster.
  targets:
    - clusterSelector:
        matchLabels:
          ash4d-lab: ""
  # correctDrift OFF, and here it matters more than usual: OpenChoreo's own
  # controllers write to objects in these namespaces as part of normal
  # operation. Turning this on before understanding which of those writes Fleet
  # would consider drift is how you get a controller and Fleet fighting over
  # the same object. Leave it off.
  correctDrift:
    enabled: false

Path 9 is enabled on the live GitRepo, but it surfaced a real bug that blocks it, and the fix is sitting in a PR I can't merge.

## What happened

I patched `spec.paths` to 9 entries. Fleet created the bundle and it failed to **target** — it never reached the cluster:

```
targeting error: cluster c-nnzn9 in namespace fleet-default:
failed to parse helm values template: template: values:10:
function "THUNDER_URL" not defined
```

Fleet pre-processes helm values as a Go template with `${` `}` delimiters. Thunder's `values.yaml` embeds that 34 KB bootstrap script the handoff flagged — 61 shell expansions (`${THUNDER_URL}`, `${username}`, …), every one of which Fleet reads as a template function call. The pre-flight `helm template` check couldn't have caught this: the collision is with Fleet, not Helm.

Fix is `helm.disablePreProcess: true` in the bundle's `fleet.yaml`. Nothing in these bundles uses Fleet templating, so it costs nothing.

**I also fixed path 18 (`observability-events`) pre-emptively** — a `grep '\${'` across `22-openchoreo/` found `${env:OPENSEARCH_USERNAME}`, the OTel collector's own syntax, which would have failed identically ten paths from now. Those two files are the only hits in the whole tree.

## Needs you

[PR #18](https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet/pull/18) — merging is blocked for me by the permission classifier. The GitRepo tracks `main` at a 60s poll, so once it merges the bundle targets on its own:

```
! gh pr merge 18 --repo darthzen/lab-fleet --merge
```

## Verified along the way

- `gateway-default` Gateway in `openchoreo-control-plane` is `PROGRAMMED=True` — Thunder's HTTPRoute has its parent.
- The control-plane Ingress already carries `thunder.ash4d.com` alongside the two working hosts.
- The CA bootstrap is **not** needed here (that's paths 10/13/15). Thunder's only ordering constraint was the CP Gateway.
- Worth noting for later commands: `rancher` is the management context where Fleet lives; the workloads are on **`sdf1`**. Querying `openchoreo-control-plane` on the `rancher` context returns an empty namespace, which looks alarming and isn't.

Say the word once it's merged and I'll watch for 9/9 and confirm `thunder.ash4d.com` stops 404ing.
